theater: 佛羅里達半島與奧基喬比湖

battle.name: 第一次塞米諾爾戰爭
battle.theater: 佛羅里達半島與奧基喬比湖
battle.brief: 一八一七年十二月十七日，傑克遜率三千人越過聖瑪麗河進入佛羅里達，發動第一次塞米諾爾戰爭。次年二月斯科特縱隊在奧基喬比湖的林地與塞米諾爾射手血戰，斯科特堡至湖區行軍約一百英里；七月美軍進佔彭薩科拉，九月宣布戰事結束。火繩槍早已退出一線序列，只餘於西班牙舊軍械庫與獵人手中。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 交戰的兩方屬於兩個截然不同的世界。美國一方以陸軍南方部為骨架：一八一七年秋，安德魯·傑克遜在紐奧良立功之後被調回，駐紮佐治亞州西南部弗林特河畔的斯科特堡，麾下有正規步兵營、炮兵連與騎兵分遣隊，另有喬治亞、田納西兩州的志願民兵與騎兵補充兵員，克里克與切羅基盟友以輔助部隊身份參戰，並有隨軍黑人士兵擔任廚役、搬運手與嚮導。西班牙在法律上仍擁有佛羅里達，但實力已經崩解：聖馬克斯與彭薩科拉的守軍缺人缺糧，一旦大軍越境便紛紛交械；英國在佛州沒有駐軍，只在海上旁觀並以外交施壓西班牙。塞米諾爾一方並非國家，而是一個聯盟：塞米諾爾人與克里克人、黑人追奴者、被解放者組成的村社聯盟，靠村社、榮譽與首領的影響力運作，主要首領有彼得·麥昆、鱷魚、喬西亞斯·弗朗西斯與科阿庫奇等。他們沒有常備軍，沒有後勤體系，戰鬥依靠村社民兵與游擊隊。
countriesEn: The two sides belonged to two entirely different worlds. On the American side stood the regular army of the United States organised as the Department of the South: in the autumn of 1817 Andrew Jackson, fresh from his victory at New Orleans, was brought back and took position at Fort Scott on the Flint River in south-western Georgia, with regular infantry companies, artillery batteries and detachments of dragoons under his orders, reinforced by volunteer militia and mounted troops from Georgia and Tennessee, by Creek and Cherokee allies serving as auxiliaries, and by black soldiers acting as cooks, drivers and guides. Spain still held Florida in law but not in fact: the garrisons of St. Marks and Pensacola were short of men and short of food, and when the invading columns crossed the border they handed over their guns more or less without a fight. Britain kept no troops in Florida and merely watched from the sea while pressing Spain diplomatically. The Seminole side was not a state but a confederacy: a league of Seminole and Creek villages, runaway slaves and people freed from bondage, run on village councils, personal standing and the influence of war leaders such as Peter McQueen, Alligator, Josiah Francis and Coacoochee. They had no standing army, no supply system, and fought through village militias and war bands.
people: 安德魯·傑克遜是這場戰爭的推手與象徵。他自一八一五年一月新奧良之戰後被調回國內，一八一七年出任南方部司令，駐地就在弗林特河畔的斯科特堡；同年六月，時任戰爭部長約翰·卡爾霍恩致函下令，要他在佛州「消滅每一個塞米諾爾人」並追回逃跑的黑人——實質上是以軍事手段處理一個外交無法解決的移民問題。威廉·溫菲爾德·斯科特中校是最重要的縱隊指揮官，一八一八年二月率隊自威拉庫奇河一線南下，在奧基喬比湖的林地血戰中以炮兵清出射擊線，那一役是全軍傷亡最重的一場。約翰·麥金托什將軍是克里克戰爭的老將，參與過一八一六年摧毀阿帕拉契科拉河畔「黑堡」之役，其後在福爾敦、奧基伊尼與黑哈奇三役中率民兵突襲村社，是鄉村攻擊的主要執行者。斯科特堡的駐軍指揮官理查德·阿布克利中校負責基地與後勤。塞米諾爾方面沒有將軍，首領多靠影響力取勝：彼得·麥昆是規模最大的戰士首領之一，鱷魚（薩姆）率小隊游擊並在黑哈奇與奧基喬比抵抗，喬西亞斯·弗朗西斯先是克里克語翻譯，後成為交涉代表，逃出莫爾特里堡的科阿庫奇則是克里克出身的塞米諾爾首領，另有比莉·鮑萊茲與麥卡諾皮等年輕戰士日後成為領袖。後世記成傳說的「鱷魚皮帶扣」，講的是一八一八年二月斯瓦尼河一帶的追擊中士兵的獵犬被鱷魚咬死，傑克遜命人剝下鱷魚皮製成腰扣。
peopleEn: Andrew Jackson was the driving force and the symbol of the war. Recalled from New Orleans, where he had fought on 8 January 1815, he took command of the Department of the South in 1817 with his headquarters at Fort Scott on the Flint River. In June of that year the Secretary of War, John Calhoun, wrote to him ordering the destruction of every Seminole in Florida and the recovery of the runaway blacks, which in practice meant using the army to settle a migration problem that diplomacy could not. Winfield Scott, then a lieutenant colonel, was the most important column commander; in February 1818 he marched his men south along the Withlacoochee and fought the battle of the hammock at Lake Okeechobee, clearing the firing line with his artillery at the cost of the heaviest American losses of the campaign. General John McIntosh, a veteran of the Creek War, had taken part in the destruction of the Negro Fort on the Apalachicola in 1816, and afterwards led militia raids on the villages of Fowltown, Okee Innee and Black Hachee, becoming the chief executor of the village attacks. Lieutenant Colonel Richard Arbuckle, commanding at Fort Scott, ran the base and the logistics. The Seminoles had no generals: their leaders drew authority from influence. Peter McQueen was one of the largest war chiefs, Alligator (Sam) led small bands and resisted at Black Hachee and at Okeechobee, Josiah Francis served first as a Creek interpreter and later as a negotiator, and Coacoochee, an escaped Creek, led Seminole bands of his own; Billy Bowlegs and Micanopy were still young warriors at the time. The anecdote that became legend, the alligator belt buckle, belongs to the February 1818 pursuit on the Suwannee, when an alligator killed a soldier's dog and Jackson had the hide made into a buckle.
kits: 火繩槍在這場戰爭裡的位置，是「已經退場的最後一代」。火繩槍是十五世紀末歐洲的技術，十七世紀初燧發槍普及之後便被軍方淘汰，到一八一七年只剩兩種身分：一是西班牙在佛羅里達的舊軍械庫裏保存的過時庫存，包括聖馬克斯與彭薩科拉的守備武器；二是獵人與老練的守備兵手上仍能使用的祖傳獵槍。真正上陣的是燧發滑膛步槍：美軍步兵使用一八一四年式與一八一七年式滑膛槍，口徑多為〇點五四英寸，配刺刀；炮兵配六磅野戰砲與十二磅榴砲；騎兵配騎槍與軍刀。一八一七年的遠征首次大量使用紙包定裝藥，但佛州雨季的濕氣令許多紙包受潮失效，這是後勤上最被低估的一項困難。塞米諾爾人的火器主要是自己鑄造與交易得來的燧發滑膛槍，也有從黑堡與美軍手中繳獲的制式槍，數量有限且缺乏火藥供應；村寨中仍可見更老式的火繩槍與火槍形制的祖傳獵槍，但只是象徵性的老物件，沒有進入戰鬥序列。裝備清單上還有騾馬與馬車、沿阿帕拉契科拉河與佛州水道運行的汽船與運兵船，以及用來追蹤獵物的軍犬——獵犬是這場沼澤戰裏最被低估的裝備之一。
kitsEn: The place of the matchlock musket in this war is that of the last generation already retired. The matchlock was a European technology of the late fifteenth century; once the flintlock became general in the early seventeenth century it was dropped by the armies, and by 1817 it survived in only two guises: as obsolete stock kept in the old Spanish armories of Florida, including the batteries at St. Marks and Pensacola, and as inherited hunting guns still in the hands of hunters and old soldiers. What actually fought were flintlock smoothbore muskets. American infantry carried the Model 1814 and Model 1817 smoothbores, mostly of .54 calibre, with bayonets fixed; the artillery brought six-pounder field guns and twelve-pounder howitzers; the cavalry had carbines and sabres. The 1817 expedition was the first to use paper cartridges in quantity, but the damp of the Florida wet season ruined many of them, an under-rated logistical difficulty. The Seminole weapons were mostly flintlock smoothbores of their own casting and of trade, together with regulation arms taken at the Negro Fort and from American soldiers, few in number and short of powder; older matchlocks and arquebus-pattern hunting guns could still be seen in the villages, but they were curiosities and never entered the line of battle. The stores lists also covered mules and wagons, steamboats and boats moving on the Apalachicola and the inland Florida waterways, and dogs used to run down game and to trail fugitives, the dogs being one of the least appreciated items of equipment in a swamp war.
tactics: 美軍的戰術底子是十九世紀初的線列與齊射：步兵排成密集橫線，齊射後裝填，再以刺刀和整齊的突進壓上去，這套做法正是卡牌上那句「方陣把弱點變成整齊彈幕」的後裔。傑克遜把部隊分成數個縱隊同時推進：一隊自佐治亞州沿斯瓦尼河東岸南下，一隊自弗林特河谷沿威拉庫奇河穿沼澤西行，另有騎兵與輔助部隊在側翼搜索。進入沼澤後，橫線被拉得極長，散兵與前哨必須頂住射擊，砲兵是唯一能對付密林的手段：奧基喬比之役，斯科特先用六磅砲向林緣直射，把藏在矮樹叢裏的射手逼出來，步兵才得以推進到林邊。塞米諾爾人拒絕會戰：他們不給美軍成列的機會，把村寨建在沼澤與密林之間，逼美軍在無路可走的泥濘裏行軍，再以精準的散射拖住推進的縱隊；他們用獨木舟沿水道轉移，夜晚退回林中，用烽火與信使在村社之間傳遞消息，並在美軍後方切斷小徑與糧道。當火力優勢無法發揮，唯一出路就是退向更深的沼澤：大沼澤地與大柏樹沼澤成了他們的堡壘，而美軍正是因此無法用一次會戰解決戰爭。
tacticsEn: The American tactical foundation was the line and the volley: infantry in a dense front, fire in ranks, then reload and advance with the bayonet in a disciplined rush, which is the direct descendant of the maxim on the card that the formation turned the weaknesses of the weapon into an orderly barrage. Jackson split his army into several columns moving at the same time: one down the east bank of the Suwannee from Georgia, one west through the swamps along the Withlacoochee from the Flint valley, with cavalry and auxiliaries searching the flanks. Once in the swamps the line had to be stretched to its limit, skirmishers and outposts had to absorb the fire, and artillery was the only answer to the hammock. At Okeechobee Scott's six-pounders first shot into the edge of the brush to drive out the concealed marksmen, and only then could his foot advance to the treeline. The Seminoles refused the set-piece battle. They never gave the Americans a chance to form line: they sited their villages between swamp and forest, forced the columns to march through mud with no road, and held the advance with accurate scattered shots. They moved by dugout canoe along the water lines, retired into the woods at night, passed news from village to village by signal fires and runners, and cut the trails and supply lines behind the columns. When firepower could not be brought to bear, the only course left was to withdraw deeper into the swamp: the Everglades and the Big Cypress became their fortress, and that is precisely why no single battle could end the war for the Americans.
data: 兵員與戰果的數字，各家記載口徑不一，只能取其量級。傑克遜的遠征軍在越境之初約三千人，隨後連同民兵、騎兵與克里克、切羅基輔助部隊膨脹到五千人上下，分成數個縱隊推進。福爾敦一役，美軍焚毀兩百座以上房舍的村落，俘獲三四百名塞米諾爾人，戰士陣亡數極少；一八一七年十二月十八日的奧基伊尼之役，美方戰報記載被襲村落約兩百人，俘獲約一百五十人，殺傷數不明。一八一八年二月十九至二十日的奧基喬比湖之戰是全戰役最慘烈的一役：斯科特部兵力約一千至一千二百人，配屬數門六磅砲；美軍陣亡約三十人、受傷約一百四十人，美方戰報稱塞米諾爾方面陣亡僅五至七人、受傷人數相若。遠征自一八一七年十二月十七日越過聖瑪麗河起，至一八一八年秋傑克遜宣布結束為止，主要作戰約九個月；縱隊由斯科特堡到奧基喬比湖的行軍約一百英里。全戰役美軍死傷合計以千人計，塞米諾爾人死於戰鬥與被俘者合計在數百量級。
dataEn: The figures for strength and losses differ from source to source and can only be taken as orders of magnitude. Jackson's invading force numbered about three thousand men at the crossing, swelling to around five thousand once the militia, the mounted volunteers and the Creek and Cherokee auxiliaries were added, and it was divided into several columns. At Fowltown the Americans burned a village of more than two hundred houses and took three or four hundred Seminoles, with very few warriors killed. At Okee Innee on 18 December 1817 the American report describes a village of some two hundred people, of whom about one hundred and fifty were captured, the number killed being unknown. The fight at Lake Okeechobee on 19 and 20 February 1818 was the bloodiest of the war: Scott commanded roughly one thousand to one thousand two hundred men with several six-pounder guns; the Americans lost about thirty killed and one hundred and forty wounded, while the American report claimed only five to seven Seminoles killed with a comparable number wounded. The campaign ran from the crossing of the St. Marys River on 17 December 1817 to Jackson's announcement of the end in the autumn of 1818, some nine months of active operations, and the column march from Fort Scott to Lake Okeechobee covered about a hundred miles. American dead and wounded over the whole war ran to a thousand men; Seminoles killed in battle and taken prisoner together numbered in the hundreds.
cause: 起因有三層。其一是一八一六至一八一七年的克里克戰爭留下的廢墟：克里克人被打散之後大批南逃佛羅里達，與塞米諾爾人、黑人追奴者以及從莫爾特里堡逃出的人混居；一八一六年美軍在阿帕拉契科拉河畔摧毀「黑堡」，這批倖存者此後全部退入佛州，成為傑克遜出兵的理由。其二是邊境現實：塞米諾爾游擊隊越過州界襲擾喬治亞邊境，擄走黑奴與牲口；美國政府要求西班牙引渡人犯，西班牙當局既無力也無意，談判數年無結果。其三是傑克遜手裡的授權：一八一七年六月，戰爭部長卡爾霍恩下令在佛州「徹底消滅」塞米諾爾人並追回逃跑的黑人，同時默許傑克遜越境進軍。表面上這是一次追捕逃奴兼報復邊境襲擊的行動，實際上是美國要奪取西班牙佛羅里達的軍事試探；佛州的主權爭議才是真正的底牌。
causeEn: The causes lay on three levels. First, the ruins left by the Creek War of 1816 and 1817: once the Creeks were broken, large numbers fled south into Florida and mixed with the Seminoles, with the runaway slaves and with those who had escaped from Fort Moultrie; after the Americans destroyed the Negro Fort on the Apalachicola in 1816, these survivors withdrew into Florida and became the stated justification for Jackson's expedition. Second, the reality of the border: Seminole war bands crossed the state line to harry the Georgia frontier and carry off blacks and livestock, the United States demanded that Spain extradite the raiders, and the Spanish authorities were both unwilling and unable, so the negotiations dragged on for years without result. Third, the authority Jackson held in his hands: in June 1817 the Secretary of War Calhoun ordered the Seminoles in Florida to be destroyed and the runaway blacks recovered, and at the same time acquiesced in Jackson's crossing of the border. On the surface this was an operation to recover escaped property and to punish border raids; in reality it was a military probe to take Spanish Florida out of Madrid's hands, and the dispute over sovereignty was the real stake.
impact: 這場戰爭把佛羅里達從西班牙手裡拿走了。一八一八年聯邦通過的追捕逃亡奴隸法例授權總統在全國任何州動用軍力追捕逃跑的奴隸，等於在法律上替越境用兵開了口子；一八一八年七月美軍進入彭薩科拉，翌年《亞當斯—奧尼斯條約》把東佛羅里達與西佛羅里達割讓給美國，1821年完成正式移交。對塞米諾爾人而言，戰敗的代價是失去佛州北部的家園：多數村社被焚，俘虜被送走，倖存者被限制在南部荒野。一八二三年《莫爾特里溪條約》劃出保留地，置於聯邦監督之下。軍事上，這場戰爭證明了一件令傑克遜不解的事：在沼澤國家裏，縱隊、縱火與佔領都管用，但決定性的會戰並不存在，傷亡在每一場小戰鬥裏累積成無法承受的數字。這一課直接餵養了此後兩個世代的小戰爭理論，也在《莫爾特里溪條約》之後埋下第二次塞米諾爾戰爭的種子。
impactEn: This war took Florida away from Spain. The federal statute of 1818 for the recovery of persons escaping from service authorised the President to use the armed forces in any state of the union, which opened the legal door for troops to cross a frontier; American troops entered Pensacola in July 1818, and the following year the Adams-Onís Treaty ceded East and West Florida to the United States, with the formal handover in 1821. For the Seminoles the price of defeat was the loss of their homeland in northern Florida: most villages were burned, the captives were sent away, and the survivors were confined to the wild country in the south. The Treaty of Moultrie Creek of 1823 set aside a reservation under federal supervision. In military terms the war demonstrated something that puzzled Jackson: in a country of swamps the columns, the burning and the occupation all worked, but a decisive battle did not exist, and the casualties accumulated in small fights into a number that could not be borne. That lesson fed the small-war theory of the two following generations, and it planted the seed of the Second Seminole War after the Treaty of Moultrie Creek.
result: 結果是美軍贏了，卻沒有一場可以拿來展示的勝負。一八一八年初的福爾敦、奧基伊尼、黑哈奇三役把佛州北部的塞米諾爾村社掃平；二月十九至二十日的奧基喬比湖之戰之後，彼得·麥昆等大首領退往大沼澤地與大柏樹沼澤，零星游擊持續到一八一八年夏末。七月，傑克遜進軍彭薩科拉，佛州全境實際落入美軍控制；九月他在斯科特堡宣布戰事結束，命令塞米諾爾人返回原居地，聲明只要回去便不再追究。命令的效果參差：部分村社接受並返回，部分則留在沼澤裏，靠遊擊與狩獵支撐到一八二三年。戰爭沒有帶來任何一次決戰，也沒有換來安寧，它只是把塞米諾爾人推到一條退無可退的路上：留在原地是第二次塞米諾爾戰爭，走進保留地是另一種喪失。
resultEn: The Americans won, yet they had no victory to display. The raids of Fowltown, Okee Innee and Black Hachee in the early months of 1818 cleared the Seminole villages out of northern Florida; after the fight at Lake Okeechobee on 19 and 20 February, the great war chiefs such as Peter McQueen withdrew into the Everglades and the Big Cypress, and scattered resistance continued until the end of the summer of 1818. In July Jackson marched into Pensacola and Florida as a whole passed into American control; in September he declared the war over at Fort Scott, ordering the Seminoles to return to their old lands and stating that those who returned would not be molested. The effect of the order was uneven: some villages accepted and came in, others stayed in the swamps and lived by hunting and raids until 1823. The war brought no decisive engagement and no peace; it only pushed the Seminoles onto a road with nowhere left to retreat, for staying put meant the Second Seminole War, and going into the reservation meant a different kind of loss.
